utterances.text: Yes. A report was filed against me which had to do with my work for a company in Republika Srpska. However, the court dismissed the charges. This involved the company called Prontes from Teslic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you recall that a criminal report had been filed against you on the 20th of March, or, rather, the 25th of March, 1996, to the police station of Stari Grad in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember that. But I explained to you that the reports had been dismissed and that I had been tried for only one crime at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On the 10th of May, 1997, again, in Belgrade, the Zemun police station, another criminal report was filed for unlawful material gain. Fraud 3; do you recall that? Fraud, Article 3.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But this was not in Zemun. I gave a statement to another police station in Belgrade for that same particular case. That was the 29th November police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Again, in 1996, in the month of June, crime 1, and that was again to the SUP of Cukarica in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: That was that same particular instance you were referring to earlier. You are confusing things.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, can we please place the document on the ELMO. We received the document today, and could we please call up 1D01-0292. We -- we translated the document into English today, and Madam Carter has been informed of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... what do you want to us do with 1D00-0103?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nothing else. I only showed part of it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Madam Carter, please do sit down, and you may talk, now that we have recognised you.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would object to cross-examination on basis of relevance for any charge that has not resulted in a conviction as the witness is clearly stating and as the document - once we see the second page - will indicate that this individual, while has certainly given statements or has been a part of previous proceedings, has not been convicted of those proceedings. This would be unfair for the witness to -- and irrelevant for him to be cross-examined on such issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we please bring back 1D01-0103 paragraph 4. Madam Carter, look that paragraph and read what the witness says. He doesn't talk about convictions; he talks about investigations.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I have been now advised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Objection overruled. You may proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have on our screens 1D01-0292. Can we scroll down in the B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sir, let me not repeat myself. You'll see that all the various criminal reports bear different dates, don't they?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I started from item 8, and then went upwards, as I was putting questions to you. At any rate, this particular letter states that six criminal investigations were conducted against you before you gave your statement to the OTP; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, but some criminal offences were dismissed in that process.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In 2003, perhaps you stated this of your own will without the Prosecutor asking you about it, you did state, however, that up until 2003 there had been no investigations conducted against you.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: No, I simply said at that time there had been no investigations going on against me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, let me read out what you said in your interview for the Prosecutor, in paragraph 4. "Other than that I have never been under investigation." You said that and signed that statement. Several days ago, when you reviewed your statement, did you not feel compelled to correct this.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Well, no. Nobody asked me about it. We started from number 92 and went through to paragraph 108.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's see what the statement says about convictions. In 2000 you were convicted by the 2nd Municipal Court of Belgrade to a sentence of imprisonment of one year. Do you remember what crime was involved in this conviction?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: The crime of fraud.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What paragraph are you reading from this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What have I been reading now is the second set of paragraphs, under number 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which are the convictions rendered against him pursuant to a final decision. This was in 2000.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Therefore, three years before your statement to the OTP; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you serve the sentence?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: All the four convictions were served as a single sentence. And, yes, I served it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And this is something that you omitted to inform the OTP of.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Nobody asked me about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The district Court of Subotica, in 2003, after you gave your statement to the OTP, passed a sentence of four months of imprisonment against you. Do you recall what crime was involved here?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: This was illicit trade, I think. But any rate the four convictions were -- I was punished for the four convictions by serving a single term of imprisonment, so I don't know why you keep going back to the various convictions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm doing this simply because I wanted to know what crime was involved. This isn't what the document states.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we turn to the next page, under 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have the Backa Topola municipal Court issuing judgement, whereby a sentence of imprisonment was rendered again.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was for the possession of weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 15th of October, 2004, the Municipal Court of Ruma, term of imprisonment of ten months; do you recall what this was?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This was the time when I drove cement for the Borovica Transport Company when we were caught transporting cement at the time when there was a ban on the transportation of such items to Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When was this?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: I was a driver in the company, and I was carrying out orders of my superiors. Since the cement works in Beocin owed a great amount of money to the company I worked of -- I worked for, we engaged in illicit trade of cement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. The document also states that you were -- your behaviour is scornful, bullyish, that you are prone to fighting. What do you have to tell us about that?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I was involved in a bar Brawl where I had to act in self-defence. Would you not do the same if you were in my shoes?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will not be commenting on what you're asking me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now tender this into evidence. We have a draft translation which could perhaps be MFIed for the time being. And in the meantime, we will procure an official version of the translation which could then be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence and marked for identification. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D92, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Now let us go back to what this Trial Chamber -- or this Court would like to hear about. I just have one more question about the period preceding your testimony. Did you report, or did you call The Hague Tribunal or Prosecutor's office, or did they actually seek you out?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: The first interview, in 2003, I was with a colleague who was in the reserve, he was called by a representative of the OTP. He mentioned me in his interview, after which I also went and had a -- an interview with the representative of the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: When you went and had the interview with the representative of the OTP, did you go of your own volition, or did he call you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As my colleague had already been called in, and this had to do with a case where he was cited as the -- as a suspect, or an accused, he asked me to come and make a statement, and I did, voluntarily, and made a statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Now I will go through your statement chronologically and specifically about your testimony in answering the questions of Ms. Carter regarding the transport of these men to the Republika Srpska in the spring of 1994. And maybe it would be best if we can have on the screens your statement; document 1D01-0103, page 18 of the B/C/S, and 19 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Paragraph 92. That's where you begin your account of that episode. And in the third line -- third sentence you say: "It should be noted that at that time the decision of the government of the Republic of Serbia to bring in all men fit for..." -- let's pause a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So again paragraph 92, if we may pull that up, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So you can see in paragraph 92 the sentence that I was reading: "It should be noted that at the time the decision of the government of the Republic of Serbia was in effect to bring in all men fit for military service, aged 18 to 65 from the RS and the RSK regardless of whether they had refugee status." Now, mentioned some of this a little earlier to Ms. Carter. And you said that at the check-point where you were, you had a dispatch from the MUP I assume?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And from this telegram or dispatch you learned that this was a decision by the government of the Republic of Serbia; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The witness, on page 55, line 11, said yes, and mistakenly it -- the answer seems to be in the negative. I can repeat the question if that is necessary. So Witness, at this check-point where you were, you were mobilized as a reserve policeman. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And that's where you saw this telegram. And you concluded on the basis of that telegram that this was a decision issued by the government of the Republic of Serbia to bring in all men fit for military service; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. At this check-point, Kosta 4, to be more precise, and I have already explained where there was, because there were a lot of check-points around Belgrade, each road leading to and out of Belgrade had a check-point. The Belgrade-Zagreb way, the Novi Sad road, the Ibarski [indiscernible] road. There were check-points on every road, and the leader, the check-point commander, brought this telegram. It was underlined in red ink and we were warned as to what we were to look for and to pay attention to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I ask you once again, sir, to please just pause for a short while. Let the interpreters finish interpreting the lawyers words, okay? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we just scroll up the document a bit? I need to see the bottom part.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you testified today, describing this episode, I understood that to mean that you only drove one such convoy, transporting people; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you say here in the last line: "These buses were escorted by the Serbian MUP." Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You make no mention at all here that there were any military vehicles there. Do you recall that during this interview with the relevant representatives of the OTP, you never mentioned any military vehicles?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: I only said that the Republika Srpska MUP escorted us to the Morovica forest where we were taken over by the Yugoslav army escort because these were the border troops of the Yugoslav army.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. So am I correct in saying that this entire trip you were escorted by the MUP escorts, and then at the Morovica wood you were met by the army of Yugoslavia, and you were escorted through the wood, and on the other side by the army of Yugoslavia; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And after you left the forest, you said, in your descriptions, that there were no more military escorts; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And the Morovica forest is on the border very close to the border with Republika Srpska, or, rather, Bosnia and Herzegovina; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Well, the Morovica forest is on the river Sava, and it is on the border with the Republic of Bosnia. And at the other end where the Bosut river is, there was also the border with Croatia. So this was precisely at the tri-border area between Serbia, Bosnia, and Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You testified today that on the bus where you transported these individuals from Bubanj Potok, there was also Lieutenant-Colonel Tomasevic whom you knew from before the war.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: At this time he was a major, and he lived in Backa Topola where he was married and had a child and an apartment where they lived. As I already mentioned before my wife was from Backa Topola, so we were good friends, we were close friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you testified today that he was in Bubanj Potok when the bus left off for Knin.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And he road with me to Knin because he hails from around Vojnici in the Republic of Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Very well. Can we just see the next page, please, in the B/C/S version, the same paragraph, 93. And as for the English version, we can see that portion on this page already. It's toward the end of the paragraph. You said when you provided your statement to the Prosecutor that: "There were three buses, including mine, left for Knin. Two buses remained in Banja Luka, and two buses left for Prijedor. On my return to Belgrade, I brought along about 25 officers and non-commissioned officers of the Yugoslav army whose shift had ended. This group included VSK Colonel Vladimir Tomasevic whom I had known from Vukovar."

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Well, this means that he -- well, what I said was that he went to Knin with me, but he did not return. So this part of the statement of 2003 is incorrect. And I knew this man from the Vukovar battlefield because he was there then because the barracks in Backa--

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have to interrupt you. You have already explained this, and I don't think that your acquaintance with him is not really that relevant. I see there is a discrepancy between what you said in your statement and what you have testified to today, and you, yourself, could see this. Now my question is this: You told us a minute ago that the Prosecutor showed you the relevant paragraphs of statement, that you occasion to read them and correct them before you began your testifying today. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I can only tell you that on the way back for Belgrade, there was some 20 to 25 officers and non-commissioned officers. I don't know exactly what the ratio was, but they returned with me to Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But in your statement of 2003, you also said that in that group that went from Knin to Belgrade, Colonel Tomasevic was in the group as well; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But in fact he remained -- remained in the army of the Serbian Krajina up until the end of 1994, and after that, he went to a command of the army of Republika Srpska in Trebinje, where he retired from.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So this part of your statement is mistakenly interpreted, and you failed to observe that error while you reviewed it; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Well, the Prosecutor didn't really pay much attention to that and neither did I. But it is true that 25 officers and non-commissioned officers returned to Belgrade with me. Now I don't know exactly the ratio. And I apologise, if I can just add one thing. You can see from my personnel file that -- or, rather, from the personnel file of Colonel Tomasevic, can you easily establish exactly when he was in the army of the Serbian Krajina and when he returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sir, would you please just stick to my questions and try to answer my questions. Please try to focus on what I am asking you about exactly and do not go beyond that. Now my next question is this: On this occasion, if I understood this correctly, there were three MUP vehicles, buses. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you recall -- can you recall the names of the other drives, the drivers who went with you? Can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: I can only remember one name, a member of MUP, but I can't remember the other name.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could we have his name, please.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Milan Markovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He was also a reserve policeman in the brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: No, he was an active duty policeman in the Serbian MUP, and he is still on duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now, do you know any of the names of the military bus drivers?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know any of the names of the non-commissioned officers or officers that escorted that bus?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Well, on my bus, there was Major Vladimir Tomasevic, but as for the other buses, I wasn't really there contact with them, and I didn't know the names. But the drivers who drove those buses did know their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So are you trying to tell us here that Major Tomasevic was your military escort on the bus?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: He was the escort, and there were two other military officers. If I recall correctly one of them was a staff-sergeant, and the other one was a warrant officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. And just one last question. So as an escort, being the escort on the bus, he remained in Knin. He didn't return?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did not return.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think this is a good time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is indeed. We'll take a break and come back at quarter to 6.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour. [Interpretation] Can we have the witness's statement back on our screens. I'm interested in paragraph 94, and can we turn to the next page in the English version, please. I will put several questions to you that I don't think were asked of you in the examination-in-chief and are very important to present things. In paragraph 94, you state: "I returned to my firm in early April 1994 and stayed there until December 1994, when I left my firm because it had gone bankrupt. I started working for the Partnertrans company from Novi Sad, owned by Nenad Mandic," et cetera, et cetera. You continued to say that this individual had connections at the ministry of transport and the Ministry of Defence. What you described for us earlier was the period while you were mobilized into the reserve force of the police, while you manned the check-point you described for us, and you also did the [indiscernible]. But then from April to December 1994 as transpires from your statement, you went back to the department store company in Belgrade; right?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But, you see, the department store company went bankrupt, and so I worked for this other transportation company.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the period between April and December 1994, on how many occasions were you mobilized into the reserve police force, if you were mobilized there at all?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Throughout the seven months, I worked at the company. Since we did not receive any salaries, I went back to the police reserve force for several months and then went to work for Partnertrans. However, you see, the Partnertrans company had its trucks requisitioned for the purposes of VJ, and that's where they were used in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. In the period you worked as a driver for the Partnertrans company, you were not mobilized for the MUP of Serbia, were you?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: No. I was a driver for the Partnertrans company. However, the truck that I drove was requisitioned and used for the purposes of the VJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. You state that this individual Mandic had connections in the ministry of transport and the Ministry of Defence, right? I suppose you're referring to the ministries of the Republic of Serbia or of the FRY?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Well, those were ministries of the FRY at that time. Mandic is the president of the association of hauliers in the ministry of transport of Serbia today.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let me ask you this: Under whose orders did you drive trucks at the time when you worked for the -- for this particular transport company?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Under the orders of the army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And who, from the army of Yugoslavia, gave you assignments?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: I was assigned to the unit 2418. There are travel orders to that effect, in all the other documentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you recall the name of any of the persons who told you to do these trips when you drove trucks in that period of time?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: I recall several individuals. One of them was a major who is now a retired lieutenant-colonel of the VJ, Jukic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter missed the first name.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You were not mobilized into a unit of the VJ at the time, were you?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the interpreter says she missed the first name of Mr. Jukic, who I see on the transcript is written as "Vukic."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you slowly repeat the first and last name of the major who issued orders or assignments to you.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Zarko Sljukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Which unit was Zarko Sljukic a member of, of MUP or VJ?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Of the VJ. He was a VJ major, and now he is a retired lieutenant-colonel of the VJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us the unit he belonged to -- which unit he belonged to at the time?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: I was a member of the unit 2418. I don't know the unit he belonged to. He was my superior.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where this particular unit was stationed?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: The unit was headquartered at the military post of Ruma.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And that's where the Partnertrans company was, or was it Borovica?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: The Partnertrans company was in Novi Sad; whereas, the Borovica transport company was located in Ruma.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In that period of time, on how many occasions did you report to Major Sljukic, and on how many occasions did you drive the truck on his orders?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: As I would come back from an assignment that I completed, I would get further assignments either by him or his deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My question was: On how many occasions back in 1994, at the time you worked for the Partnertrans company in Novi Sad did the VJ approach you with a request to drive for their purposes.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Roughly 10 to 15 times. The truck was assigned to that particular unit and did trips as required by the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This individual Mandic who was the owner of Petratrans --

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Partnertrans.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... did he provide his trucks for the purposes of the VJ simply because he would get certain benefits for that?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The vehicle that you used and in respect of which you received orders, was it in fact used for the purposes of the Ministry of Defence?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: I can't say clearly whether it was used by the Ministry of Defence or by the VJ. I know that the -- that sanctions were imposed on the Republic of Serbia. Companies could not send their vehicles abroad, and they had to make due in order to conduct their business.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The route you described in order to traverse the crossing of Raca, you said that the EU monitors were present at the border crossing at Sremska Raca, in the territory of the FRY.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As you went round the border crossing, reached the bridge, and got into the Republika Srpska, there was also a border crossing there which was called Bosanska Raca?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And it was within the jurisdiction of the Bosnian police and customs officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you claim that no European monitors were present there; right?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The transportation of fuel you referred to, you repeatedly participated in these convoys, did you not?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You give quite a transparent testimony of these events at page 21 of the B/C/S; page 24 of English, paragraph 107. I will read out the relevant part of your statement. I quote: "The oil transport was organised by Dusan Borovica through his firm, Borovica Transport, headquartered in Ruma. I personally took part in the transport of fuel from Bulgaria to the Republika Srpska via Serbia. This began in 1992, but I personally took part that this operation in 1994." A moment ago we heard that you had worked for that company owned by the gentleman from Novi Sad in 1994.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Nedjo Mandic. And I worked there up until October of 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. What I'm interested in next is the shipment of oil from Bulgaria. Who was your employer at the time?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: The Borovica transport company, owned by Dusan Borovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This particular job of work you did had nothing to do with your engagement in MUP, had it?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You go on to say, and I quote: "The drivers were given cash for their daily expenses, for bribing customs officers, and for buying fuel." Is that right? Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who gave you -- the money to you as a driver as you went to do this shipment?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: I was given the money by the -- by the owner of the company, Dusan Borovica, or from his brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You go on to explain the procedure, and you say, I quote: "The tanker trucks would normally be taken to the parking lot, and as we would be doing that there would be -- while the fuel was being pulled over, a DB unit Sremska Mitrovica or Ruma would come there." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: From this portion of your statement, which you had occasion to read, it follows that you were hired by a private businessman, Dusan Borovica. He gave you the money; you went to Bulgaria, purchased oil; you transported it to his parking lot, from where it was transported to Republika Srpska or Republic of Serbian Krajina, in an organised fashion. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You continued to say in 108, paragraph 108: "20 percent of the invoiced amount" -- invoiced amount probably meaning the amount that was received from the sale of oil "was paid to the Ministry of Defence and the Ministry of Trade." Do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: The oil and oil products that were imported were imported on the order of the Centreks company registered by the government of Republika Srpska. The representatives of Centreks company, Slobodan Beatovic, would be waiting for us at the border as well as Branko Sutalo, who still today works for the Republika Srpska government. Government.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And in your -- according to you a percentage went to the Ministry of Defence and the Ministry of Trade of the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: All the cash flow went through the accounts of that company. Some of the fuel was set aside for the purposes of the VRS, and other funds were deposited into the accounts of the Ministry of Defence of Republika Srpska. And the remaining portions were divided by -- or were taken by those who provided escort for the convoy. They had a share that they took.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As you said, it was the state security of Serbia that provided escorts.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. The SDB provided escorts as well as Arkan's Men. Arkan came to the premises of Borovica Transport Company or Arkan's Men came to Borovica Transport Company on several occasions, and they would be the ones doing the job as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Based on what you have just stated and what you have just confirmed, in this whole process of purchasing oil from Bulgaria, in none of these elements does the army of Yugoslavia feature, does it?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You also mentioned that fuel was purchased from Romania, and that it was actually smuggled across the Danube; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And in -- in none of that does ever the army of Yugoslavia feature, does it?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us only clarify, this fuel was purchased illegally in the market of Romania and then -- and was then illegally transported to Republika Srpska and the RSK?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was illegally purchased from certain individuals, and the transportation of fuel would be escorted all the way to the Borovica forest. Let me only state that this section of the road through the Borovica forest was at all times under the control or escort of the army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You have already told us this. Let me ask you one other thing. At one point in your statement, you said that for a while you participated in the smuggling of cigarettes. I have a very simple question: Do you know whether the assets originating from the smuggling of cigarettes, some of the assets ended up in the budget of the RSK and the RS?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, all the goods imported into the RS went through the Centreks company which was registered and founded by the government of the RS, and then they distributed these goods.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And who did you receive orders regarding this smuggling activity?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was the owner of the company, because I was an employee of the Borovica company.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's now go back to another issue, and it has to do with the transport of ammunition that you mentioned today. My question is this: You described today, during your testimony, that, on several occasions, you transported ammunition and military equipment from the plants of Kragujevac factory, the military in industry, or rather, from the military industry manufacturers from Federal Republic of Yugoslavia; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: During the proofing that you had with the Prosecutor, and it reads as follows in English, as Ms. Carter said, or interpreted your statement and you have signed it. It reads as follows. Let me just see if I can find that portion. That's in paragraph 15 of the proofing notes and the information report dating a few days ago, or yesterday. [In English] [Previous translation continues] ... carried out, came from weapons factory and warehouses in Serbia. The factories were Zastava Kragujevac, Milan Blagojevic in Lucani, Prvi Partizan in Uzice, Sloboda in Cacak, Trajal Krusevac, and Krusik in Valjevo, and Prva Iskra, Baric. [Interpretation] Now, as I've read this, does this jog your memory, which of these manufacturers did you go to, to transport the ammunition and materiel?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: I went to Zastava, then to Prvi Partizan, and the military depot in Gorjani near Uzice, and the military depot near Gornje Milanovac called Brdjani. And once I also took goods from a depot near Vrnik [phoen], and once from Grmec. I can't recall exactly what type of goods.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You further say in the report [In English] [Previous translation continues] ... "includes 4 July barracks in the Belgrade garrison, the barracks in Bubanj Potok, a military warehouse in Gorjani, a military warehouse Vrnik near Novi Sad, Paracin and Brdjani near Gornje Milanovac, among others." [Interpretation] In the next paragraph you say as follows -- or, rather, the Prosecutor says in his notes [In English] [Previous translation continues] ... "due to his previous work he worked for the department store which sold weapons and ammunitions. He has also been previously deployed with the MUP and VJ." [Interpretation] This report that I have just read out to you makes no mention that you went to these military depot, but, rather, that you knew of them from before, while you used to work for the department stores.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: No. I went to Zastava and the Pari Partizan in Uzice, Gorjani, Brdjani, and Vrnik. And Ms. Prosecutor just wanted me to clarify how it was that I knew anything about the military industry from earlier on, in Krusik and Prvi Partizan. And because I was a driver for the department stores, Rovnik Kucik [phoen] company, they had also departments that sold weapons, side-arms, and that's how I came to go there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's what I understood, too, based on your statement to Ms. Carter, but you never said to Ms. Carter that you actually went to those military depots.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Actually, I did tell her that I went to Gorjani, Brdjani, and once in Tovarnik. I know that my colleagues also went to Paracin, but I never went there, nor did I ever go to Prva Iskra, but I know that some of my colleagues did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now once you get to the military depot, do you remember, did you actually receive transportation papers, including a bill of lading which would list all of the goods that have to be loaded?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We would get a bill of lading with all the items that we were loading, and then we would also hand in the documents and the goods on the border, where Ranko Sljukic and Slobodan Beatovic met us, and then they would tell the trucks where to go to download this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me just ask you this. Once you arrived to the site where you're supposed to unload your truck, would anyone sign for the reception of this load or these items?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Well, no. There were always people from Republika Srpska or from the Centreks company, and they would check all of this. They would join us, they would join us, get on our trucks in Dvorovi, and then they would go to the place where these -- where the truck would be unloaded.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, was there any document, any paper trail as to what happened with these items, where they were unloaded?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Well, the individual who escorted us, he would receive the bill of lading, on the spot, and sometimes this would be a representative of the Centreks company and sometimes a representative of Republika Srpska. They would receive all the papers and keep them. So the entire documentation was kept by Republika Srpska or by the Centreks company, because they would receive all of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now, the Centreks company, is, if I remember, a company that was actually established by the authorities of Republika Srpska; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please pull up -- or show paragraph 103 on the screens. So if we can go back a few pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now in paragraph 103 it says: "The truck drivers were civilians, but they were attached to the VJ or the Ministry of Defence. In principle, they worked for the Ministry of Defence. Nedjo Mandic and Dusan Borovica provided transport services to the Ministry of Defence and received certain benefits from the ministry." Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you did not have a military assignment while you were working at the Borovica company; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I did have my military assignment at the time was at the MUP of Serbia, but I was not called up to do any military exercises or anything of that sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, maybe I wasn't precise enough. But you didn't have an assumed in the army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: No. But while I was driving the trucks, I worked for the Ministry of Defence and for the army because they worked together with the drivers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But as you mentioned here, they were all with the Ministry of Defence; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They were assigned to the Ministry of Defence, and they received all the -- issued all the orders and forwarded them to us, telling us what to transport and where to, et cetera. There were also other trucks from Autotransport in Valjevo and Juga Ekspres from Leskovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You've got a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a moment. There's another portion of your statement that I would like to put to you. While we were discussing the transport of oil products, you said that one of the sources where you obtained the fuel was from Bulgaria and Romania. But do you recall that crude oil was sent from Djelatovac to the refinery in Pancevo?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But the crude oil was transported to Pancevo by Sidtrans from Sid and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the second company from Sid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't hear the name of the second company from Sid.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat slowly.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Sidtrans.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, we've got Sid transport already in the first answer. Is it -- is it Sid Transport or Sidtrans? What are the two companies, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was Borovica transport and Sidtrans from Sid. In addition there were also tanker trucks owned by Zeljko Raznjatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Dzeletovci were in Srpska Krajina?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Djeletovci was on the territory of the Republika of Srpska Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And that is where the plants for the refining of crude oil were; correct? Or, rather -- that were later sent to Pancevo for refining.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is where the crude oil was obtained, and then it was sent for refining to the Pancevo refinery.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you don't know what the arrangements were between the Republic of Serbian Krajina, who owned these plants, and the Pancevo refinery, what type of financial arrangements. You don't know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that. I just know that the sources were under the control, including the ones in Dzeletovci of the Skorpions units, these units were established by the security service of the Republic of Serbia, and a portion of those -- a portion of those sites were also secured by Arkan's units.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Lukic. Any re-examination, Madam Carter?

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And you may remain seated.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Sir, at page 55 today you were discussing how you learned about the decision by the government to bring in the able-bodied men who were from the RS and the RSK. Do you recall such testimony?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. When I returned to the MUP unit I was assigned as I've already mentioned to the check-point at Kosa 4. The check-point commander at the time - if you like, I can give you his name - he was the commander of this check-point and our superior officers. He brought, that morning, a telegram, and then he underlined in red ink the portions that we were supposed to pay special attention to.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Your Honour, based upon the cross-examination of this witness on this point, I would like to present a couple of documents to the witness, two of which there are on our 65 ter list, one of which we just received from Serbia pursuant to a RFA that's included on our eighth supplement list. These were not listed as -- or excuse me, as documents to be used in this examination. But due to the fact that this issue was brought up on cross-examination, we would ask leave of Court to be able to use them now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have a problem specifically, because I received this document for the first time now, while my cross-examination was under way. This document was not discovered to us, and I don't object to any document that was on a 65 ter list to be used if they were disclosed earlier, but this document was disclosed to me in the course of my cross-examination, which means that it was added to the 65 ter list during my cross-examination, and I think this is not the procedure that we should follow. I don't think we should put to the witness a document that we had -- knew nothing about before our cross-examination began.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you talking about -- when you say "this document," is that the document that Madam Carter refers to as recently received as a result of an RFA?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is what she has just said, and I have no information as to when she received this document. I don't know anything about that. It's quite possible that it is the way you put it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Carter, what document did you give to this gentleman?

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the document has a 65 ter number of 0647-6864. Ms. Javier is looking right now to see exactly when it was disclosed to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is that the same document, sir? Mr. Lukic, does it have the same 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Apologies, Your Honour, that is an ERN number, not a 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Does it have the same ERN number? You called it a 65 ter number. Are you getting no translation, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am getting translation, Your Honour, but I can't ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... [Microphone not activated] [Overlapping speakers] ... What is the ERN number of that document, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The ERN number of this document that I have in my hand now, if that is the document that Ms. Carter would like to use, is 0647-6864.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, that document was disclosed. We received the translation. It was disclosed on May 8th, and it's part of the Prosecution's eighth supplemental 65 ter. Specifically, we gave it the preliminary number, and we'd the Court to give it the final number of 65 ter 9534.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, when you say it was disclosed on the 8th, disclosed to the Defence, or is it listed in your eighth supplemental 65 ter list?

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: It was disclosed to the Defence on May 8th -- excuse me, on April 9th, and then a part of the eighth supplemental request which was on May 8th, 2009.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Apparently, the document is alleged to have been disclosed to you on the 9th of April, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've just been informed that the document was disclosed to us on the 9th of April, and in that sense, I can just try and clarify what I've said earlier. Since we have not responded to the supplementary list, nor has the Trial Chamber ruled on that, irrespective of that in view of the fact that Ms. Carter would like to put it the witness now for the first time and that we did not receive any information regarding this document, I think we should have the right to also question the witness about this document, once Ms. Carter has done that, because we did not receive information that she will use the document during the examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah. You are referring to 8th of May when the supplemental 65 ter list was being filed. The document is supposed to have been disclosed to you a month earlier, on the 9th of April. That's -- and you have confirmed that. You have confirmed that just now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I'm not confirming that. Maybe there is just a confusion with the dates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... look at page 78, line 2, sir. That's you speaking there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document was disclosed to us on the 9th of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam, now, I don't know what your -- Madam Carter said it was disclosed to you on the 9th of April; it was included in the 65 ter -- the eighth 65 ter supplemental list on the 8th of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, I -- could you please just --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: My apologies, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic, I'm saying to you, just look at what Madam Carter said, and can you respond to that? She says you were -- this document was disclosed to you on the 9th April, and on 8th of May it was put on the supplemental list that still has to be ruled upon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have been informed by my case manager, Your Honours, that this document was disclosed to us in batch 315, and that it was disclosed on the 8th of May. In other words, on Friday, a few days ago. That it was disclosed on the 8th of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's your word against Madam Carter's on that point. But this changes the position from the initial position that you put. It was not disclosed to you for the first time during your cross-examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. The information --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... what's your argument now against Madam Carter's desire to use that document, given that it was disclosed to you on the 8th of May and not during your cross-examination today?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My argument is as follows. I do not object to Ms. Carter using the document. However, in view of the fact that you have not ruled on whether this document will be admitted, based on the 65 ter list of the 8th, I think the Defence should have the right to question, to put some additional questions to this witness if it so wishes after Ms. Carter has finishing questioning him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Very well, then, Mr. Lukic. Do you have any response on that very last point, Madam Carter?

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. The Prosecution would have no objection to the Defence having additional cross-examination on that limited purpose with regards to that specific document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Very well. Then you may proceed and put the documents that you want to put to the witness, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: I would first like to call up 65 ter 3311.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're appearing to have some technical difficulties, that it needs to be released.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Your Honour, for -- it appears that 65 ter 3311 has not been uploaded into e-court. We do have hard copies of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What's this document that's on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: That would be 65 ter 3311, Your Honour. I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Sir, in your testimony at page 55, you indicated that your order actually came from the Republic of Serbia. The document that we have before us that -- that is from the Republika Srpska indicates that a meeting took place between a -- or a meeting was to take place between a representative of Yugoslav army General Staff, MUP, Serbia, MUP Republika Srpska, the minister of Defence of Republika Srpska, as well as the head of the administration of the army of the Republika Srpska Main Staff. Sir, were you aware that the VJ was also involved in the rounding up of able-bodied men to send them back to the RS and the RSK?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot see in what way the document has anything to do with the issue. If the Prosecutor wanted to suggest to put a leading question to the witness, she could have done so without showing the document to the witness, who is not aware of it. I think that by formulating her question thus, Madam Carter has in fact suggested the answer to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Your objection is that the -- Madam Carter is asking a leading question. Madam Carter.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Respectfully, Your Honour, a leading question by definition implies that an answer is being suggested. I'm simply asking the witness, is he aware that the army of Yugoslavia was also involved in a decision --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Carter, if you put a document on the screen which tells him the answer before you put the question, you're putting a leading question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: I am guided, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Objection sustained.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: We can remove the document from the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Sir, were you aware of who made the decision to round up the able-bodied men to send back to the RS and the RSK?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic. I know what you're going to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness was shown a portion of the statement, and he provided a specific answer to that question. The government of the Republic of Serbia. It is not me testifying now. I'm merely reminding my learned friend of his answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I already said in my statement that a telegram had reached the check-point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah. Sir, when the counsel are arguing between themselves, stay out of it until you -- they address themselves to you. Anyway, what the nub of your argument is what he is saying. The question has been answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. He provided the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the answer has been given.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: If I may have just a moment to consult with counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You do.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Sir, are you aware of any commendations to the participants in the roundup of the able-bodied men by the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: In my statement, I said that a telegram had reached the check-point which had the -- the dispatch had been issued by the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia, pursuant to the instructions issued by the government of the Republic of Serbia to the effect that the able-bodied men from the RS and the RSK should be rounded up at certain locations, i.e., police stations, from where they were transported either to the VJ barracks. In our case, they were transported to the police station where they were subjected to a medical check and transported onwards.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I understand that that is what happened at the inception of this process. Are you aware of any commendations or any comments on this roundup after the fact?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: That's something that I cannot speak about. What the sort of cooperation existed between the government of the Republic of Serbia and the governments of the RSK and RS. I only know that the decree was being followed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, sir, please do listen to the question. You're not being asked anything about cooperation between the Republika Srpska and the Republic of Serbia. You are being asked whether you aware of any commendations to the participants in the rounding up of these able-bodied men. If you don't understand the question, ask the lawyer to repeat himself or reformulate it. Don't give an answer that is not an answer to the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I'm not clear on is where would they be arriving from, the commendations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Carter, that's for you.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Sir, are you aware of any commendations from any source, for the men who participated in the roundup?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: I know that when we were manning check-points, we had to, at the end of your shifts, make a list of the individuals that were taken in, and -- and the events that happened. Whether any of our superiors received commendations from higher levels is something I'm not aware of.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. At page 65 today, you were discussing with Defence counsel, the pass at Bosanska Raca, specifically whether European commission monitors were present.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: I would ask that your statement be brought up. I'm sorry, I don't have the Defence exhibit number of that. At paragraph 99, specifically at paragraph 20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's 1D01-0103. It has not been tendered.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me try it this way.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Sir, you indicated that there were no custom officers present -- I'm sorry, no European monitors present at that time. Were European monitors anywhere near that bridge?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: No. The monitors were present at the border crossing itself, where the police of the Republic of Serbia and the customs service of the FRY were present. That was at the Sremska Raca border crossing itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Sir, were the European monitors aware of the crossing at the bridge?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: The European monitors could not have been aware of the crossing at the bridge, because the border crossing was 3 kilometres away from the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Outside of the distance of the bridge, were any other measures taken to prohibit the European monitors from knowing that the crossing was occurring?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Since the crossings would take place at night, between 1.00 and 3.00 a.m., the volume of traffic was quite low, and it was on the Serbian side near Kuzmin where the police of Serbia would stop the traffic; whereas, in Republika Srpska, the Republika Srpska police would stop all traffic on the section of the road between Dvorovi and the point where the border was crossed.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Was anything else done?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm -- I -- I object the fact that the witness is being shown his statement while the questions are put to him. I would like the statement to be taken off the screen while he is answering questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: I have no objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the statement please be removed from the screen. Yes, Madam Carter.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Sir, at the border crossing -- excuse me. In relation to the European monitors, were there -- outside of the methods that you have already described, were any other methods used to avoid detection of the convoy?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: In my statement from 2003, I enclosed a sketch of the Sremska Raca-Bosanska Raca border crossing and the route taken by the convoys. There, the border was clearly depicted as well as the location of the Serbian police, customs officers, European monitors, including stalls selling audiocassettes with music. There were cafes there as well. There was a cafe on the border crossing on the Serbian side, as well as on the other side of the border to the right; there was another cafe there. I said that the bridge was some 3 kilometres away from the border crossing itself. The road went up the hill, and the trucks in the convoy would switch their lights off so that the European monitors would not be able to observe them. At the same time, in order to drown out the sound of the engines, the stalls selling audiocassette would play loud music.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Who was manning these stalls?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Civilians. Persons who owned these stalls.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: How would these civilians know to begin the music at that time?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: They were informed by the police deployed at the border crossing.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. And, finally, at page 72 of today's transcript, you were asked about who was responsible for the convoys, and specifically it was suggested that the Ministry of Defence was the sole responsible party. Sir, when drivers were attached to VJ or MUP vehicles, who paid their salaries and benefits for the time in which they served on those convoys?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: In my case specifically, I received my salary from the MUP of the Republic of Serbia, both my salary and daily allowance. As for those who were on the convoys for the VJ, it must have been the VJ that paid their salaries, or their home companies, depending on what the arrangement was.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I appreciate your answers, and I pass the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Lukic, are you happy?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since the document was not involved, I don't have any further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sir, that brings us to the conclusion of your testimony. Thank you so much for taking your time to come and testify at the Tribunal. You are now excused; you may stand down, and please travel we will back home, okay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon, I see you rising.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, the next witness is a closed session witness. I note the time. I believe he is still speaking with a colleague of mine. Could we adjourn until 2.15 tomorrow and begin the witness at that time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Indeed. The Chamber stands adjourned to tomorrow, 2.15 in the afternoon in Courtroom I. Court adjourned.
